C01.title: Hala'ib Triangle
C01.text: Egypt claims Hala'ib under the 22nd parallel of the 1899 agreement, and Sudan under the 1902 administrative line. Egypt has run the area since the 1990s.

sources.title: UN Security Council, 812th meeting, S/PV.812 (1958)
Letter from Sudan to the Security Council, S/2017/791
Letter from Egypt to the Security Council, S/2017/953

C02.title: Bir Tawil
C02.text: Each country's line from the Hala'ib dispute gives Bir Tawil to the other, so neither claims it.

sources.title: US Department of State, International Boundary Study No. 18, Egypt-Sudan boundary (1962)
Bir Tawil, Wikipedia

C03.title: Ilemi Triangle
C03.text: Kenya administers the Ilemi Triangle up to the 1950 patrol line, and South Sudan disputes it. The two agreed in 2019 to set up a joint border commission but have not settled the border.

sources.title: Ilemi Triangle, Wikipedia
East African Herald, 2019
Eye Radio, 2019

C04.title: India-China disputed areas (XXX)
C04.text: Demchok, Jadh-Nelang, Kaurik and Lapthal-Barahoti lie on the India-China boundary. In a 1993 agreement both countries undertook to respect the Line of Actual Control pending a boundary settlement.

sources.title: India-China Agreement on the Line of Actual Control (1993), UN Peacemaker
Sino-Indian border dispute, Wikipedia

C05.title: India-China line between Nepal and Bhutan
C05.method: GAUL line as cut line, ends joined to the UN boundary
C05.text: The 1890 Anglo-Chinese Convention set this Sikkim section of the India-China border on the watershed between the Teesta and the Mochu.

sources.title: Convention between Great Britain and China relating to Sikkim and Tibet (1890), UK Treaty Series 1894 No. 11

C14.title: Kuril Islands in the Russian Federation
C14.text: The Soviet Union took the southern Kurils in 1945. Russia administers them, and Japan claims them.

sources.title: Treaty of Peace with Japan (1951), UN Treaty Series No. 1832
Joint Declaration by the USSR and Japan (1956), UN Treaty Series No. 3768

C07a.title: Bassas da India
C07a.text: Bassas da India is one of France's Scattered Islands in the Mozambique Channel, a district of the French Southern and Antarctic Lands, and Madagascar claims it.

sources.title: UN General Assembly resolution 34/91 (1979)
IEDOM, Portrait des TAAF

C07b.title: Europa Island
C07b.text: Europa Island is one of France's Scattered Islands in the Mozambique Channel, a district of the French Southern and Antarctic Lands, and Madagascar claims it.

sources.title: UN General Assembly resolution 34/91 (1979)
IEDOM, Portrait des TAAF

C07c.title: Glorioso Islands
C07c.text: The Glorioso Islands are one of France's Scattered Islands in the Mozambique Channel, a district of the French Southern and Antarctic Lands, and Madagascar claims them.

sources.title: UN General Assembly resolution 34/91 (1979)
IEDOM, Portrait des TAAF

C07d.title: Juan de Nova Island
C07d.text: Juan de Nova is one of France's Scattered Islands in the Mozambique Channel, a district of the French Southern and Antarctic Lands, and Madagascar claims it.

sources.title: UN General Assembly resolution 34/91 (1979)
IEDOM, Portrait des TAAF

C07e.title: Tromelin Island
C07e.text: Tromelin, east of Madagascar, is one of France's Scattered Islands, a district of the French Southern and Antarctic Lands, and Mauritius claims it.

sources.title: Note from France to the UN Secretary-General on Tromelin (2009), UN DOALOS
Note from Mauritius to the UN Secretary-General on Tromelin (2011), UN DOALOS
IEDOM, Portrait des TAAF

C08.title: Chagos Archipelago
C08.text: The United Kingdom runs the Chagos Archipelago as the British Indian Ocean Territory, and Mauritius claims it. A 2025 treaty would recognise Mauritian sovereignty and let the United Kingdom keep the Diego Garcia base for 99 years, but it is not in force.

sources.title: ICJ advisory opinion on the Chagos Archipelago (2019)
UN General Assembly resolution 73/295 (2019)
UK-Mauritius agreement concerning the Chagos Archipelago (2025), not in force
Al Jazeera, 2 October 2026

C09.title: Ashmore and Cartier Islands
C09.text: Ashmore and Cartier Islands are an Australian external territory in the Timor Sea, where a 1974 agreement lets traditional Indonesian fishers work.

sources.title: Ashmore and Cartier Islands Acceptance Act 1933
Australia-Indonesia memorandum of understanding on traditional fishermen (1974), FAOLEX

C10.title: Clipperton Island
C10.text: Clipperton is a French possession in the eastern Pacific under the direct authority of the French government, which delegates powers there to the High Commissioner in French Polynesia.

sources.title: Arbitral award on Clipperton Island (1931), UN Reports of International Arbitral Awards
French National Assembly, report No. 4219 on the status of Clipperton (2016)

C11a.title: Akrotiri
C11a.text: Akrotiri is one of the two Sovereign Base Areas the United Kingdom kept in Cyprus under the 1960 Treaty of Establishment.

sources.title: Treaty concerning the Establishment of the Republic of Cyprus (1960), UN Treaty Series No. 5476

C11b.title: Dekelia
C11b.text: Dekelia is one of the two Sovereign Base Areas the United Kingdom kept in Cyprus under the 1960 Treaty of Establishment.

sources.title: Treaty concerning the Establishment of the Republic of Cyprus (1960), UN Treaty Series No. 5476

C12.title: Northern Ireland
C12.text: ISO 3166 lists the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland as one country (GB), with Northern Ireland as its subdivision GB-NIR.

sources.title: ISO 3166: GB
UN M49 standard country list

C15.title: China parts that likely belong to Taiwan Province of China
C15.text: Kinmen, Lieyu and the Matsu islands lie off Fujian and are administered from Taipei.

sources.title: Kinmen, Wikipedia
Matsu Islands, Wikipedia

C16.title: China parts that likely belong to Democratic People's Republic of Korea
C16.text: The 1962 China-DPRK border treaty gave each river island to the side whose people lived on or farmed it, otherwise to the nearer bank, and most Yalu islands went to the DPRK.

sources.title: China-DPRK boundary treaty (1962), Chinese Wikisource
China-North Korea border, Wikipedia
Hwanggumpyong Island, Wikipedia

C17.title: Finland parts that likely belong to Åland Islands
C17.text: In 1921 the League of Nations left Åland with Finland as a self-governing territory, and the Åland Convention of 20 October 1921 neutralised it. ISO 3166 lists it on its own (AX).

sources.title: Åland Convention (1921), League of Nations Treaty Series No. 255
ISO 3166: AX
UN M49 standard country list

C18.title: Micronesia (Federated States of) parts that likely belong to Marshall Islands
C18.text: Enewetak and Ujelang are the westernmost atolls of the Marshall Islands.

sources.title: Marshall Islands baselines and maritime zones (2016), M.Z.N.120.2016.LOS, UN DOALOS
Micronesia-Marshall Islands maritime boundary treaty (2006), UN DOALOS

C19.title: Russian Federation parts that likely belong to Ukraine
C19.text: Tuzla Island in the Kerch Strait is part of Crimea, which Russia has held since 2014. UN General Assembly resolution 68/262 calls on states not to recognise any change to Crimea's status.

sources.title: UN General Assembly resolution 68/262 (2014)

C20.title: Bonaire parts that likely belong to Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic Of)
C20.text: The 1978 Venezuela-Netherlands boundary treaty puts Las Aves (Aves de Sotavento), east of Bonaire, on Venezuela's side.

sources.title: Venezuela-Netherlands boundary delimitation treaty (1978), UN DOALOS

C21.title: Angola parts that likely belong to Democratic Republic of the Congo
C21.text: The 1891 Brussels convention between Portugal and the Congo Free State runs the lower Congo border along the navigation channel and names Mateba, Bulabemba and the Princes islands on the Congo side.

sources.title: US Department of State, International Boundary Study No. 144, Angola-DRC boundary (1974)

C22.title: Kazakhstan parts that likely belong to Russian Federation
C22.text: Kazakhstan and the Russian Federation signed their border treaty on 18 January 2005, and it entered into force on 12 January 2006.

sources.title: Kazakhstan-Russia state border treaty (2005), UN Treaty Series No. 52717

C23.title: Japan parts that likely belong to Senkaku Islands
C23.text: Taishō-tō (Chiwei Yu) is the easternmost of the Senkaku Islands, which Japan administers and China claims.

sources.title: China, baselines of Diaoyu Dao and its affiliated islands (2012), M.Z.N.89.2012.LOS, UN DOALOS
Note from Japan on M.Z.N.89.2012.LOS (2012), UN DOALOS
Senkaku Islands dispute, Wikipedia

C24.title: Russian Federation parts that likely belong to Finland
C24.text: Finland ceded a number of Gulf of Finland islands to the Soviet Union in 1940, and the 1947 Paris Peace Treaty confirmed that border.

sources.title: Treaty of Peace with Finland (1947), UN Treaty Series No. 746
Finland-USSR agreement on the Gulf of Finland (1965), UN DOALOS
Moscow Peace Treaty (1940), Finnish Treaty Series 3/1940

C25.title: Greece parts that likely belong to Türkiye
C25.text: Article 12 of the 1923 Treaty of Lausanne keeps islands less than three miles from the Asian coast under Turkish sovereignty.

sources.title: Treaty of Lausanne (1923), League of Nations Treaty Series No. 701

C26.title: Canada parts that likely belong to Hans Island
C26.text: Canada and Denmark both claimed Hans Island until a 14 June 2022 agreement split it between Canada and Greenland.

sources.title: Joint statement by Canada and Denmark at the 32nd Meeting of States Parties to UNCLOS (2022)
Library of Congress, The Hans Island agreement (2022)

C27.title: Eritrea parts that likely belong to Doumeira Islands
C27.text: Djibouti and Eritrea both claim Ras Doumeira and Doumeira Island. They fought there in 2008, and Qatari observers held the area from 2010 to 2017.

sources.title: UN Security Council resolution 1862 (2009)
Report of the Monitoring Group on Somalia and Eritrea, S/2017/925

C28.title: Gabon parts that likely belong to Equatorial Guinea
C28.text: Gabon holds Mbanié and nearby islets. In May 2025 the International Court of Justice found that the title Spain held in 1968, to which Equatorial Guinea succeeded, is the one with the force of law.

sources.title: Report of the International Court of Justice 2024-2025, A/80/4
ICJ, Land and Maritime Delimitation and Sovereignty over Islands (Gabon/Equatorial Guinea)

C29.title: Iran (Islamic Republic of) parts that likely belong to Abu Musa and Tunb Islands
C29.text: Iran took the Greater and Lesser Tunbs on 30 November 1971 and, under a memorandum of understanding with Sharjah, part of Abu Musa. The United Arab Emirates claims all three.

sources.title: UN Security Council, 1610th meeting, S/PV.1610 (1971)
Letter from the United Arab Emirates to the Security Council, S/1996/693
Peace Palace Library, The Tunbs and Abu Musa

C30.title: New Caledonia parts that likely belong to Hunter and Matthew Islands
C30.text: France administers Matthew and Hunter islands as part of New Caledonia, and Vanuatu claims them. In 2026 Vanuatu filed an application at the International Court of Justice, which cannot proceed unless France consents.

sources.title: ICJ press release 2026/22, Vanuatu files an application concerning a dispute with France
PINA, 2026

N-XCO.text: Conejo is a small island in the Gulf of Fonseca that the 1992 International Court of Justice judgment on the El Salvador-Honduras border did not address. Honduras has personnel there, and El Salvador claims it.

sources.title: ICJ, Land, Island and Maritime Frontier Dispute (El Salvador/Honduras)
Conejo Island, Wikipedia

N-XGR.text: Banc du Geyser is a mostly submerged reef north of Madagascar that France holds with the Glorioso Islands. Madagascar and the Comoros claim it.

sources.title: Banc du Geyser, Wikipedia

N-XIK.text: Greece holds Imia (Kardak), two islets off Bodrum, which it says Italy ceded with the Dodecanese in 1947. Türkiye disputes this, and the two nearly went to war over them in January 1996.

sources.title: Treaty of Peace with Italy (1947), UN Treaty Series No. 747
US Congressional Research Service, Greece and Turkey: the rocky islet crisis (1996)
Imia, Wikipedia

N-XLR.text: The Republic of Korea holds the Liancourt Rocks (Dokdo, Takeshima) in the Sea of Japan, and Japan claims them.

sources.title: Liancourt Rocks dispute, Wikipedia
Republic of Korea, Ministry of Foreign Affairs: basic position on Dokdo
Japan, Cabinet Secretariat: Japan's response on Takeshima

N-XMA.text: Canada staffs the lighthouse on Machias Seal Island, and the United States claims the island under the 1783 Treaty of Paris.

sources.title: Machias Seal Island, Wikipedia
ICJ, Delimitation of the Maritime Boundary in the Gulf of Maine Area (Canada/United States)

N-XMR.text: Tonga claimed the Minerva Reefs in 1972, and Fiji told the UN in 2018 that the area is in dispute.

sources.title: Tonga: Proclamation on the Minerva Reefs (1972), FAOLEX
Note from Fiji to the UN Secretary-General on Tonga's submission (2018), UN DOALOS

N-XPA.text: Perejil (Parsley) Island lies off Morocco near Ceuta. After a Moroccan landing in July 2002, Spain and Morocco agreed to leave it empty, without settling sovereignty.

sources.title: Dawn, 2002
Perejil Island, Wikipedia

N-XSA.text: Belize holds the Sapodilla Cayes, and Honduras claims them. Belize took the case to the International Court of Justice in 2022, and in 2026 the Court allowed Guatemala, which also claims them, to intervene.

sources.title: ICJ press release, Belize v. Honduras (2022)
ICJ, Sovereignty over the Sapodilla Cayes (Belize v. Honduras: Guatemala intervening)

D-XDE.text: India administers Demchok west of the Charding Nullah and China administers Dêmqog east of it, and each claims the whole sector.

sources.title: India-China Agreement on the Line of Actual Control (1993), UN Peacemaker
Demchok sector, Wikipedia

D-XJN.text: India administers the Nelang valley in Uttarkashi district, Uttarakhand, and China claims it as part of Zanda County, Tibet.

sources.title: India-China Agreement on the Line of Actual Control (1993), UN Peacemaker
Nelang, Wikipedia
Sino-Indian border dispute, Wikipedia

D-XKU.text: India administers Kaurik in Lahaul and Spiti district, Himachal Pradesh, and China claims it as part of Zanda County, Tibet.

sources.title: Kaurik, Wikipedia
Sino-Indian border dispute, Wikipedia

D-XLB.text: India administers the Barahoti plain and the Lapthal and Sangchamalla pastures in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand, and China claims them as Wure. The two governments held talks on Barahoti in New Delhi in 1958.

sources.title: Barahoti, Wikipedia
Sino-Indian border dispute, Wikipedia

D-XSP.text: Shipki La is a pass on the Sutlej between Kinnaur district, Himachal Pradesh, and Tibet, and China claims an area on the Indian side near it. The 1954 India-China agreement on trade with Tibet names Shipki La as a pass open to traders and pilgrims.

sources.title: Agreement between India and China on trade and intercourse between the Tibet Region and India (1954), UN Treaty Series No. 4307
Sino-Indian border dispute, Wikipedia
Shipki La, Wikipedia

D-XCH.text: India administers Chumar in southeastern Ladakh, and China claims land south and southeast of it. Troops from both countries faced each other there in September 2014.

sources.title: Dawn, 2014
Chumar, Wikipedia

D-XCE.text: Chumar East is part of the Chumar sector in southeastern Ladakh, on the Pare Chu near Chepzi, where India's and China's claim lines differ.

sources.title: Chepzi, Wikipedia
Chumar, Wikipedia

D-XKO.text: Benin and Burkina Faso both claim Kourou/Koalou near their tripoint with Togo. In May 2009 the two governments declared it a neutral zone under a joint committee, pending referral to the International Court of Justice.

sources.title: leFaso.net, 2009
Koalou, Wikipedia

D-XCR.text: The Congo River between Brazzaville and Kinshasa is the boundary between the Republic of the Congo and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. A 1908 declaration delimited the line in Stanley Pool (Pool Malebo), and elsewhere in the channel it is not fixed.

sources.title: US Department of State, International Boundary Study No. 127, Congo-Democratic Republic of the Congo boundary (1972)

D-XMO.text: Where the Moselle, Sûre and Our form the border between Germany and Luxembourg, the rivers are common territory under the joint sovereignty of both states, as set out in their border treaty of 19 December 1984.

sources.title: Germany-Luxembourg border treaty (1984), UN Treaty Series No. 45359

D-XMB.text: France and Italy differ over about 65 hectares around the summit of Mont Blanc. Italy holds that the boundary follows the watershed across the summit, and France that the summit lies wholly in France.

sources.title: US Department of State, International Boundary Study No. 4, France-Italy boundary (1961)
Mont Blanc, Wikipedia

D-XIB.text: Brazil administers Brazilian Island at the confluence of the Quaraí and Uruguay rivers, and Uruguay claims it. The 1851 boundary treaty gives the islands at the mouth of the Quaraí to Brazil, and Uruguay holds that the island lies in the Uruguay River.

sources.title: US Department of State, International Boundary Study No. 170, Brazil-Uruguay boundary (1979)
Brazil-Uruguay border, Wikipedia

D-XKA.text: India administers Kalapani in Pithoragarh district, and Nepal claims the land east of the Mahakali River under the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli, including Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhura. Nepal added the claim to its map and Constitution in 2020.

sources.title: Nepal, Ministry of Foreign Affairs: response on Lipulekh (2025, Nepali)
India, Ministry of External Affairs: weekly media briefing on Lipulekh (7 May 2026)
Kalapani territory, Wikipedia

D-XDS.text: The Dramana and Shakhatoe valleys in western Bhutan are part of the Bhutan-China boundary talks, held since 1984. The talks follow a 1998 agreement to keep the status quo and a 2021 memorandum on a three-step roadmap.

sources.title: Bhutan, Ministry of Foreign Affairs: press release on the three-step roadmap (2021)
China, Ministry of Foreign Affairs: China and Bhutan sign MoU on a three-step roadmap
Bhutan-China border, Wikipedia

D-XKT.text: This section of the Kyrgyzstan-Tajikistan border between Kok-Tash and Khoji A'lo, near a shared water intake, stayed undelimited after 1991, and clashes began there on 28 April 2021. The two countries signed a treaty on their whole border on 13 March 2025, in force since 31 March 2025.

sources.title: UN Secretary-General on the Kyrgyzstan-Tajikistan Treaty on the State Border (13 March 2025), UN Kyrgyzstan
Fergana, Kyrgyzstan-Tajikistan border treaty comes into force (2025)
2021 Kyrgyzstan-Tajikistan clashes, Wikipedia

D-XLE.text: This section of the Kyrgyzstan-Tajikistan border in Kyrgyzstan's Leilek district stayed undelimited after 1991, and the 2021 clashes reached villages there. The two countries signed a treaty on their whole border on 13 March 2025, in force since 31 March 2025.

sources.title: UN Secretary-General on the Kyrgyzstan-Tajikistan Treaty on the State Border (13 March 2025), UN Kyrgyzstan
Fergana, Kyrgyzstan-Tajikistan border treaty comes into force (2025)
2021 Kyrgyzstan-Tajikistan clashes, Wikipedia

D-XVO.text: Land use and roads northwest of Vorukh, a Tajik exclave inside Kyrgyzstan's Batken region, were disputed after 1991 and figured in the 2021 clashes. The two countries signed a treaty on their whole border on 13 March 2025, in force since 31 March 2025.

sources.title: UN Secretary-General on the Kyrgyzstan-Tajikistan Treaty on the State Border (13 March 2025), UN Kyrgyzstan
RFE/RL, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan's border agreement (2025)
Fergana, Kyrgyzstan-Tajikistan border treaty comes into force (2025)
